title: Trump Fires Inspectors General Across Federal Agencies in January 2025
description_short: Trump fired inspectors general at multiple federal agencies in a late-night January 2025 move.
description_medium: On January 24, 2025, President Donald Trump fired inspectors general at multiple federal agencies in a late-night move. The Associated Press reported that roughly 17 watchdogs were dismissed, with the firings effective immediately. The available reporting does not support this record’s separate claim about June dismissals of senior FBI agents or identify the Defense and Intelligence Community inspectors general in that June episode.
description_long: On the night of January 24, 2025, President Donald Trump dismissed inspectors general serving at multiple federal agencies. The Associated Press reported the next day that roughly 17 independent watchdogs had been fired and that the dismissals were effective immediately. Trump confirmed the action to reporters aboard Air Force One and said he would put “good people” in the positions. Inspectors general oversee agency operations and investigate waste, fraud, abuse, and violations of law. The contemporaneous report noted questions about statutory requirements for advance notice to Congress; this draft does not characterize the removals as unlawful because that conclusion requires legal analysis beyond the event description. This is the January 2025 inspector-general action. It does not substantiate the original record’s separate June claim about senior FBI agents or inspectors general specifically at Defense and the Intelligence Community, nor the claim that the firings eliminated the last internal checks. Those claims should remain excluded unless a June-specific source identifies the officials and supports the asserted consequences.

title: Trump Pardons Faustino Bernadett
description_short: Trump pardoned Faustino Bernadett on January 19, 2021; DOJ lists his federal conviction, sentence, fine, and surrender date.
description_medium: The Justice Department records President Donald Trump’s January 19, 2021 pardon of Faustino Bernadett. Its clemency table lists a Central District of California conviction for misprision of a felony, a 15-month prison sentence, one year of supervised release, a $60,000 fine, and a February 26, 2021 surrender date. The record does not explain the pardon decision.
description_long: The Justice Department’s clemency record states that President Donald Trump pardoned Faustino Bernadett on January 19, 2021. DOJ identifies a Central District of California case and a conviction for misprision of a felony. The clemency table lists a 15-month prison sentence, one year of supervised release, a $60,000 fine, and a surrender date of February 26, 2021. The separate grant document confirms the pardon date and summarizes the case and sentence. These records support a factual account of the pardon and the listed court disposition. They do not describe the conduct behind the conviction, explain why Trump selected Bernadett, or document an exchange, favoritism, or corruption. The prior “Corrupt Pardons” classification therefore is not supported by the supplied evidence and is removed from this proposed draft. The neutral title describes the established event without implying a motive. A case narrative or contemporaneous clemency rationale would be needed to make claims about the underlying conduct or reason for clemency.
